_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `LowpolyMutation` is a semio-NATIVE vocabulary carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no oracle is registered and the decision below records what stands in for one.

oracles.rationale:
A second implementation of the `s.lowpoly.lowpoly` document and all seventeen typed mutations, in Python, at `../🧪️tests/mutate-lowpoly-1/🐍️.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` (the two members and the shape of an object), rules 2, 3 and 7 of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md` — the id-keyed object collection, the INDEX-keyed paint-layer collection with `insert`/`remove`, and absolute `move`/`rotate`/`scale` — and the seventeen committed `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintets, which are the only statement of three things: that this subset tags its mutations EXTERNALLY, the payload being `{"MoveObject": {…}}` with a PascalCase variant name as its single key where every sibling subset in this repository tags internally with a `"mutation"` member; that `edit-paint-layer` splices base64 RUNS into the layer's pixel buffer at byte offsets, overwriting in place and never resizing it; and that `create-mesh` carries a `meshWorkspace` argument the snapshot does not hold at all. The reference decodes and re-encodes the base64 pixel buffers itself and inverts an edit by capturing the same byte ranges out of the pre-mutation buffer, which is exact precisely because the verb never resizes the layer. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. This registration SUPERSEDES the `lowpoly-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision, whose argument — that the two-level addressing "is this subset's own specification, not a fact an external mesh or scene library could confirm or refute" — was refuted in this same wave by `mutate-fem3d-1` and `mutate-gisterrain-1`, which took Python second implementations over this same carrier. Two levels of addressing are not an obstacle to a second implementation; they are something a second implementation must model. A THIRD-PARTY library was declined, not merely absent: no mesh or scene format models a paint stack addressed by index inside an object addressed by id, and none of them reads this carrier. ALL SEVENTEEN KINDS ARE ADJUDICATED AND NONE IS REFUSED: the mesh child handle carries the caller's own `childId`, so nothing here depends on a content-addressing function no specification states. ONE CEILING ON WHAT THIS COMPARISON ESTABLISHES: the SUBJECT half does not run this subset's codec — `../🧪️tests/mutate-lowpoly-1/🦀️.rs` links no plugin crate and replays the committed vectors — so today it establishes that an independent implementation of the specification computes the committed after-snapshots, not yet our codec against a second producer. A `lowpoly_mutation_report_json` bridge beside the mutation enum closes it; it is not added here for two reasons, and neither is that the verb is hard: it is PRODUCTION code in a crate this test-side pass deliberately does not touch, and it could not be verified end to end today anyway. `parity` was not measured for any case in this pass: the single-case probe `parity exhaustive --owner 🗒️note --case mutate-note-1` was killed at the runner's OWN 900 s per-case budget while still COMPILING the generated subject host — the runner's message names the cause, shared cargo target-dir lock contention from a concurrent session — and then threw `spawnSync cargo ETIMEDOUT` out of `runProbe` with no summary line at all. `📓️w14-final-audit.md` §5.3 measured the underlying blocker one day earlier (`unresolved import component::component_persistent_local` in `semio-framework-plugin`, which sits in every generated host's dependency graph); this pass did NOT re-verify whether that is still the state, and says so rather than repeating it as fact. This subset's own plugin crate compiles clean at `cargo check --lib`. This case also reads no real-world artifact: all 85 of its fixtures are handcrafted specification vectors. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `lowpoly-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 17-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

[2026-09-02, D1 — SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION] Promoted from cross-semio-implementation to verified-native-second-implementation: this artifact is semio-native (isSemioNativeArtifact), this reference's own third-party survey above (kept verbatim) already names what was checked and declined, its python implementation differs from the Rust subject, and it covers 100% of this manifest's 1 capability/capabilities with 17 committed fixture vector(s). See .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION/📓️d1-native-oracle-discharge.md.

candidatesConsidered.reason: no mesh or scene format models a paint stack addressed by index inside an object addressed by id, and none of them reads this carrier.

oracles.rationale: Pillow 12.2.0 is already importable from this repository's `.venv` as a transitive dependency of the declared development dependency `matplotlib`; this third-party-library oracle therefore adds no dependency. It serves exactly `roundtrip-png` in `../🧪️tests/io-lowpoly-png-1`: the Rust subject first calls the real `serialize_bytes()` and hands its exact PNG byte stream to the Python adapter. `PIL.Image.open` independently decodes that subject artifact and verifies PNG identity, width, height, RGBA pixel format and byte length, decoded RGBA pixels, and the `semio-lowpoly-dsl` `tEXt` keyword. It neither constructs a substitute PNG nor derives or compares lowpoly's DSL text. The fixture exercises the documented 1×1 opaque-white fallback because its first paint layer is only eight bytes; the document itself remains losslessly retained in PNG metadata. The other eight stdio formats remain covered by the `lowpoly-io-native-round-trip` no-oracle decision.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: Ticket 26/08/29/LOWPOLY-END-TO-END-COMMANDS-IO-AND-MUTATIONS, `🧪️tests/io-lowpoly-1`: round-trips the committed `LowpolySnapshot` fixture through this subset's own `serialize_bytes` and `deserialize_bytes` for the eight non-PNG stdio formats `dwg`, `gltf`, `json`, `las`, `obj`, `ply`, `stl` and `txt`. `LowpolyObject.mesh` is a content-addressed handle, not embedded geometry, so `dwg`, `gltf`, `las` and `stl` are explicit architectural-limit stubs while `json`, `obj`, `ply` and `txt` retain the document through their own format mechanisms. The case preserves the metamorphic export-then-import law so each format becomes green only when its real implementation exists. PNG is deliberately excluded from this decision: `io-lowpoly-png-1` sends the actual Rust exporter bytes to the third-party Pillow oracle `lowpoly-io-png-pillow`, which independently decodes the raster and metadata container.

Ticket 26/08/29/LOWPOLY-END-TO-END-COMMANDS-IO-AND-MUTATIONS, `🧪️tests/command-lowpoly-1`: this subset's editor command surface (`../../✏️editor/🎮️commands/**`, 47 commands across 13 groups, declared by the `semio_framework_plugin::app_commands!` macro invocation in `../../✏️editor/🦀️.rs`) is native application dispatch logic, not a document format or a mutation vocabulary — there is no third-party library, CLI or standards-reference tool that models `app_commands!`'s own generated dispatch enum. The originally intended evidence — dispatching a representative command per group against a known starting snapshot and asserting the `LowpolyMutation`/`LowpolyConfigMutation` it produces — needs `ArtifactView<'_, LowpolySnapshot>`/`ConfigView<'_, LowpolyConfig>` (both defined in `semio_framework_plugin`) to construct the arguments every `handle(payload, doc, cfg, ctx)` and `LowpolyCommand::dispatch` takes, and `protocol::Mutation::diff`/`apply` (both defined in `protocol`) to apply the produced mutation and observe its effect. Neither `semio_framework_plugin` nor `protocol` is a Cargo dependency of any generated Rust test host in this repository today: `materializeRustHost` (`🧰️framework/…/🧪️tests/📜️cript.ts`) links exactly `semio-repo-test-host` (dependency-free by design), the case owner's own `sut` crate found by walking up from the case's owner directory, and `contributedOraclePackages` resolved from an `oracleHostPackages` array declared in an ancestor-scoped `🔣️oracle.json` — and no owner in this repository currently declares `semio-framework-plugin` or `protocol` there (`grep -rl "ArtifactView\|ConfigView" --include="🦀️.rs" ✏️s | grep 🧪️tests/` returns nothing repository-wide). Fixing this needs either lowpoly's own `✏️editor/🦀️.rs` to publicly re-export `ArtifactView`/`ConfigView`/`Emit`/`Fault`/`HistoryView`, or a new ancestor-scoped `oracleHostPackages` entry naming both crates — both outside the file ownership this pass was granted, so recorded as a handoff item. What this case asserts instead: `LowpolyCommand::TOOL_JOB_IDS`/`command_id()` are plain INHERENT items the macro generates (no trait import needed), so a representative payload per group constructs with its documented example shape and reports the exact manifest id this ticket's own `📝️editor-commands.md` inventory and the crate's own `every_command()` test both name — real evidence against a payload field rename or a row moving to a different id, though not against a `handle()` regression.
